2. In Writ Petition No. 6460 of 2007 the Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the orders dated 19-7-2007 (Annexure-G, G-1 and G-2) passed by the respondent No. 3 on the ex-Bond Bills of Entry No.  238393, No. 238396 and No. 238397 all dated 12-7-2007 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and why they should not be directed to assess the petitioner's goods imported under Letter of Credit No. 5647141502 dated 21-5-2007 (Annexure-B) on the basis of the zero rate of Customs duty as in force on the date of presentation of the ex-Bond Bills of Entry dated 12-7-2007 (Annexure-G, G-1 and G-2). 

 8. Thereafter the petitioner submitted into-Board Bill of Entry No. 2345709 dated 3-7-2007 for warehousing the imported goods. The petitioner thereafter submitted three ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007, which were allocated numbers as ex-Bond Bills of Entry No.  238393, No. 238396 and 238397 all dated 12-7-2007 for releasing the imported goods by way of assessment of applicable duties and taxes, if any. 

 9. Even though there was no customs duty lived by the Government on 12-7-2007 as envisaged in section 30(b) of the Act, the respondent No. 3 by its orders dated 19-7-2007 ("impugned orders") written on the face of the said ex-Bond Bills of Entry demanded payment of 5% customs duty though the respondents have however assessed and released the petitioner's similarly imported Crude Palm Olein on 5-7-2007 without any demand of purported customs duty 

 11. In Writ Petition No. 6461 of 2007 the Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the orders dated 19-7-2007 (Annexure-"G", "G-1" and "G-2") passed by respondent No. 3 on the ex-Bond Bills of Entry No. 236206, No. 236209 and No,236211 all dated 4-7-2007 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and why they should not be directed to assess the petitioner's goods imported under Letter of Credit No. 050507010018 dated 17-4-2007 (Annexure-B) on the basis of the zero rate of customs duty as in force on the date of presentation of the ex-Bond Bills of Entry dated 4-7-2007 (Annexure-"G", "G-1" and "G-2"). 

 16. The petitioner submitted that into-Bond Bill of Entry No. 235711 dated 3-7-2007 for warehousing the imported goods. 

 17. The petitioner thereafter submitted three ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007, which were allocated numbers as ex-Bond Bill of Entry Nos.236206, 236209 and 236211 all dated 4-7-2007 for releasing the imported goods by way of assessment of duties and taxes. Even though there was no customs duty levied by the Government on 4-7-2007 as envisaged in section 30(b) of the Act, the respondent No. 3 by its orders dated 19-7-2007 ("impugned orders") written on the face of the said ex-Bond Bills of Entry demanded payment of 5% customs duty though the respondents have however assessed and released the petitioner's similarly imported Crude Palm Olein on 5-7-2007 without any demand of purported customs duty. 

 19. Mr Fida M Kamal, the learned Senior Counsel along with Mr Md Ashraful Hadi and Mr Abdullah M Hasan, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners placed before us the writ petitions and the annexures thereof and submits that by the impugned orders demanding 5% customs duty is illegal and should liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority inasmuch as, no customs duty levied by the Government was in force under the Finance, Act, 2007 on the dated of presentation on ex-Bond Bills of Entry (i.e. on 12-7-2007) as envisaged under section 30(b) of the Act. The learned Senior Counsel further submits that the impugned orders are liable to be declared to have been passed with-out any lawful authority inasmuch a the impugned orders have been issued in violation of Article 83 of the Constitution. He further submits that the petitioner submitted the ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007 and on that day the customs duty was 0% but the respondent-customs authority without considering the said provision of law issued the impugned orders imposing 5% customs duty without assigning any cogent reason whatsoever, which is manifestly arbitrary and indicates non-application of mind thus the same should be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 20. Mr Kamal Next submits that the impugned orders are liable to be declared to have been passed without jurisdiction in as much as, the impugned orders have been passed in abuse of executive power for ulterior motive as because settled principle is that the goods should be assessed on the basis of the duty which was existent on the date of presentation of the Bill of Entry and since the Finance Act, 2007 exempted the duty from the imported goods and the duty was 0% from 1-7-2007 and since the petitioner submitted ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007 the imposition of 5% customs duty was illegal and the same should be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect. Thus he prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 22. Mr SM Moniruzzaman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that no customs duty would be applicable upon CPO imported under HS Code No. 15-11-10.100 which came in to effect from 1-7-2007 under the Finance Act, 2007. The importer got the goods released Vide in into Bond Bills of Entry after provisional assessment and in Bond Bills of Entry were presented on 30-5-2007 and as per rule the final Bill of Entry has to be submitted within 15 days from the date of into Bond Bill of Entry but in fact same were submitted after expiry of 33 days from the date of in Bond Bills of Entry i.e. on 4-7-2007 and as such the respondent-customs authority imposed 5% CD and 15% VAT rightly. He further submits that the petitioner submitted his in Bond Bill of Entry on 3-6-2007 but the Ex-Bond Bills of Entry were submitted on 3-7-2007 after 30 days whereas the Ex-Bond Bills of Entry were required to have been submitted within 15 days from the date of provisional in bond and in such circumstances the goods were needed to have been assessed as per order and at the rate which was prevalent at the last fiscal year. 

 23. The learned Assistant Attorney-General further submits that in fact in order to get benefit of 0% rebate as declared in budget 2007-2008 the petitioner willfully submitted his Ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 3-7-2007 for evading 5% tax and the petitioner has definite knowledge that in the next budget the loan will be imposed only 0% and after declaration of budget the petitioner submitted Ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 3-7-2007 thus he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 26. Admittedly after arrival of the goods at Chittagong Port, the petitioner submitted the relevant ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 3-7-2007 when the customs duty 0% and 5% customs duty has already been withdrawn by the Finance Act, 2007 from 1-7-2007. 

 27. It is settled that the customs duty should be levied on the basis of the duty which was in existence at the presentation of the Bill of Entry and since the petitioner submitted his ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 3-7-2007 and on that day customs duty was 0%, the decision of the respondent customs authority was illegal and the same should be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal. 

 28. The petitioner submitted Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007 and in the meantime 5% customs duty for the imported goods has already been withdrawn by the Finance Act, 2007 from 1-7-2007. 

 29. It is well settled that the assessment should be made on the basis of the duty, which was in existence on the date of presentation of the Bill of Entry. In the instant case admittedly Bills Entry were submitted on 4-7-2007 and the Government though stated in their affidavit-in-opposition that the imported goods arrived at Chittagong Port on 31-5-2007 but the respondent in their Affidavit-in-opposition admitted that the petitioners submitted their ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007 for getting the benefit of 0% customs duty. 

 30. Since the petitioners submitted their ex-Bond Bills of Entry on 4-7-2007 when the customs duty was 0%, the customs authority was under obligation to assess the goods on the basis of 0% customs duty. This principle is supported by the latest decisions of our Apex Court in the case of Esquire Electronics Ltd vs Bangladesh reported in 59 DLR (AD) 91. Wherein their Lordships held: "It is now a settled principle of law whatever may be the position on the date of opening the Letter of Credit but the importer is saddle with the liability to the taxes and duty prevalent on the date of filing of the Bill of Entry". 

 31. So as per decision of our Apex Court the assessment orders dated 19-7-2007 passed by the respondent No.  3 imposing of 5% customs duty instead of 0% duty which was in existence on the presentation of the ex-Bond Bills of Entry are illegal and the same should be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 In the result, both the Rules are made absolute however, without any order as to cost. The impugned orders dated 19-7-2007 passed by the respondent No. 3 imposing 5% customs duty instead of 0% which was in existence on the presentation of the ex-Bond Bills of Entry are hereby made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect. The respondent-Customs Authority is hereby directed to assess the petitioner's goods under Letter of Credit No. 5647141502 dated 21-5-2007 (Annexure-B to the writ petition No. 6460 of 2007) and under Letter of Credit No. 050507010018 dated 17-4-2007 (Annexure-B to the writ petition No. 6461 of 2007) on the basis of the zero rate of customs duty which was in force on the date of presentation of the ex-Bond Bills of Entry all dated 4-7-2007. The respondents are hereby directed to release the Bank Guarantees in accordance With law if submitted by the petitioner.
